design.affected_system: privacy-preserving infectious-disease surveillance and response operations
alternatives: protect minimum coverage before needs-based allocation of infectious-disease prevention and treatment resources
adapt allocations using observed demand, uptake, and capacity for infectious-disease prevention and treatment resources
pair clinical-priority and minimum-access allocation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Case, syndrome, testing, wastewater, vaccination, and care records have explicit definitions and delays.
No individual identity or protected health information enters public release artifacts.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: retain the current distribution rule for infectious-disease prevention and treatment resources.

constraints.description: The infectious-disease public-health operations allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: communicable-disease director and public-health operations chief
design.decision_question: How should constrained supplies and service capacity be allocated under clinical and equity priorities?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The infectious-disease public-health operations allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for infectious-disease prevention and treatment resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.
independence_key.primary_outcome: eligible need without assigned service capacity

design.intended_claim: A versioned allocate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting infectious-disease prevention and treatment resources, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: eligible need without assigned service capacity
distributional gap in eligible need without assigned service capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report allocated doses or slots as administered treatment or health benefit.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for infectious-disease prevention and treatment resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

design.title: Allocate vaccines, tests, treatment, and outreach
transportability_risks: Pathogens, immunity, clinical practice, reporting, testing, and public behavior differ.
Surveillance changes can mimic epidemiological changes.

family.affected_system: privacy-preserving infectious-disease surveillance and response operations
claim_boundary: Area exposure, service, and vulnerability records do not diagnose individuals or prove harm.
Operational allocations are proposed planning outputs, not delivered clinical or social services.
Health-effect claims require outcome panels, identification, privacy, and external review.
family.decision_owner: communicable-disease director and public-health operations chief
family.description: Eight operational decisions for surveillance diagnosis, workload forecasting, preparedness investment, service siting, supply allocation, clinic scheduling, surge stress, and evaluation.
family.title: Infectious-disease public-health operations

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
